name: What pool resurfacing problems are cosmetic versus structural?

mainEntity.name: How can a homeowner tell whether a rough, stained, or cracked surface is just wear or a deeper pool shell problem?
mainEntity.text: How can a homeowner tell whether a rough, stained, or cracked surface is just wear or a deeper pool shell problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every bad-looking pool surface means the shell is failing. Cosmetic issues include discoloration, mild roughness, surface scale, and shallow etching that mostly affect appearance and comfort. Structural concerns are more serious and may show up as hollow-sounding spots, recurring cracks, visible separation between layers, active leaks, or movement around steps and benches. Those signs can indicate bond failure, shell movement, or plumbing-related problems that resurfacing alone will not solve. Before committing to a finish, homeowners should have the pool inspected for soundness and leak clues, especially if the pool has been empty, patched repeatedly, or resurfaced before. If the issue is only cosmetic, a new finish may be enough. If the shell is compromised, the project may need extra repair work first. That distinction protects the budget and improves the odds that the new surface lasts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cosmetic problems usually affect appearance only, such as staining, minor roughness, or shallow etching. Structural problems are more serious and include hollow spots, persistent leaks, spreading cracks, or delamination. A pool that changes shape, loses water quickly, or sounds hollow in areas needs a closer inspection before resurfacing.
